channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula mantém vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro, aponta Datafolha
item.description: Lula (PT) leads with 41% of voting intentions in the likely first-round scenario for the 2026 presidential election, according to a Datafolha poll. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) follows with 31%, maintaining the same level as in the previous survey. Lula's advantage over the senator remains practically unchanged.

item.title: Datafolha 2º turno: Lula tem 47% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 43%
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on June 20 shows Lula with 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 43% in a hypothetical 2026 presidential runoff, unchanged from the May 22 survey. Flávio Bolsonaro slightly leads in rejection at 46% versus Lula's 45%. In alternative matchups, Lula leads Ronaldo Caiado (47%-41%) and Romeu Zema (48%-39%).

item.title: Ritmo de escalada de críticas de Caiado a Flávio Bolsonaro é calculado por campanha
item.description: PSD presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado is gradually escalating his criticisms of FLávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s presidential nominee, in a calculated manner to avoid triggering resistance among Bolsonarist voters who might otherwise support him. The strategy hinges on polling trends: as Caiado gains visibility, he plans to harden his rhetoric without excessive concern for backlash. The goal is to retain Bolsonarist support while differentiating himself from his rival.

item.title: Eleições 2026: PT quer replicar encontro nacional de evangélicos pelos Estados
item.description: The PT plans to replicate nationally the evangelical leadership meeting held in Brasília, with state-level agendas leading up to the 2026 elections, aiming to expand evangelical support for Lula’s government. While avoiding direct church appearances due to fear of backlash and to uphold the separation of religion and politics, the party seeks common ground on issues like religious centers’ role in treating chemical dependency. This comes amid persistent evangelical resistance to Lula, with 62% disapproval according to an Indexa poll.

item.title: André do Prado lança pré-candidatura ao Senado ao lado de Tarcísio e Flávio
item.description: São Paulo state deputy and Legislative Assembly President André do Prado (PL-SP) launched his pre-campaign for the Federal Senate today in Guarulhos, alongside Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The event highlights the growing alliance between PL leadership and the state government ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Mais um teste para a popularidade artificial de Lula
item.description: Lula's popularity has been improving since his meeting with Donald Trump at the White House on May 7, following the rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF. The government has intensified electoral-friendly measures to regain public support, according to O Antagonista.

item.title: Eleições brasileiras já movimentam consulado em… Portugal
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential elections are already generating movement at the Brazilian consulate in Lisbon, Portugal, with increased inquiries and requests related to overseas voting. The exclusive subscriber article highlights early engagement from the Brazilian diaspora in the electoral process. Full access requires registration via the publication’s link.

item.title: ‘Brasil sem medo’: PL recomendou a Flávio Bolsonaro foco total na segurança pública
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro launched the 'Brazil Without Fear' plan, focused on public security, proposing to classify PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, lower the age of criminal responsibility to 16, punish those over 14 for serious crimes, build five prisons modeled after El Salvador’s, and add 500,000 prison slots in four years. The plan follows a visit to Donald Trump and allied advice to prioritize security in the campaign, exploiting Lula’s weakness in this area, where 47.6% rate federal performance as poor.

item.title: Petistas divergem sobre estratégia de busca por voto independente para favorecer Lula
item.description: Some Lula campaign coordinators argue for abandoning efforts to win independent voters through policies like income tax exemptions up to R$5,000 and ending the 6×1 work scale, calling them ineffective due to entrenched rejection of Lula. Instead, they propose focusing attacks on Flávio Bolsonaro on social media to increase his rejection among independents, as both candidates exceed 50% rejection and independents make up 32% of the electorate, per a recent Quaest poll.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro reage a enteados com versão ‘bela, recatada e do lar’
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro has scaled back her involvement in Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential campaign, stating she prioritizes caring for her husband, Jair Bolsonaro, after facing criticism from her stepchildren, who pressure her to confine herself to domestic duties. She has adopted a 'beautiful, reserved, and homemaker' posture, avoiding political events and waiting for the 'right moment' to act, while her stepchildren seek to undermine her influence over the Bolsonaro political legacy.

item.title: Mendonça barra impulsionamento pago pelo PL contra Lula nas redes sociais
item.description: Minister André Mendonça of the TSE barred the Liberal Party (PL) from boosting a negative video on social media that links President Lula to criminally investigated individuals and criminal factions, while also criticizing his stance on classifying PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist groups. The ruling aims to prevent the spread of potentially misleading content during the electoral period. Full access to the article requires a subscription.

item.title: Fala de Lula sobre Neymar viraliza em redes sociais na China
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's comment calling Neymar the "world's first home office call-up" due to the player's injury and absence from the tournament went viral on Chinese social media, particularly Weibo, generating hundreds of comments. While some found the remark humorous, most defended Neymar and criticized Lula, noting the player's past public support for former President Jair Bolsonaro. On the same day, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) defended Neymar in a video, also criticizing the Lula administration's spending on luxury travel and hotels.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro sai em defesa de Neymar após fala de Lula: 'Só um deles tem espaço no coração do brasileiro'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro defended footballer Neymar after President Lula mocked his absence from Brazil’s first two 2026 World Cup matches, calling him the 'first home office call-up'. Bolsonaro praised Neymar as a humble-origin star who inspires youth and runs social projects, stating that Brazil supports the player and that only one of the two holds a place in the hearts of Brazilians.

item.title: A estratégia ‘a conta gotas’ do plano de governo de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign plans to roll out its government plan incrementally, starting with announcements on public security and combating criminal factions. The strategy aims to build a positive, proposal-driven image and attract female voters with specific policies in the coming weeks. The goal is to counter resistance reflected in recent polls.

item.title: “Neymar é craque e Lula é presidente turista”, diz Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro defended Neymar Jr. in a social media video, criticizing President Lula's comments about the player's absence from the Brazilian national team. He labeled Lula a 'tourist president' and praised Neymar's talent, reinforcing his public image as a Bolsonaro-aligned figure.

item.title: Brasil encaminha classificação na Copa com vitória sobre o Haiti
item.description: Brazil defeated Haiti 3-0 in the World Cup, with goals from Matheus Cunha (2) and Vinicius Jr., earning four points in two matches and putting the team in a strong position to advance to the knockout stage. Coach Carlo Ancelotti praised the team's performance, noting improvements in attack and defense, and confirmed Neymar is expected to be available for the upcoming match against Scotland. The United States also secured qualification with a 2-0 win over Australia.

item.title: 🚨 TRUMP DE OLHO EM LULA E MORAES | PTMASTER EXPLODE | PRESOS DO 08/01 ESQUECIDOS? | ELEIÇÕES 2026 📱
item.description: The video claims Donald Trump is monitoring the actions of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Alexandre de Moraes, criticizing the alleged neglect of those imprisoned following the January 8, 2023 events. Associated with the PTMASTER channel, it frames the situation as political persecution and questions the impartiality of Brazil’s judiciary, linking these issues to the 2026 elections.

item.title: Master, pauta-bomba e big techs: 9 fatos que você precisa saber para terminar a semana
item.description: The Master case investigation targeted PP president Ciro Nogueira, Senate president Davi Alcolumbre, Chamber president Hugo Motta, and government Senate leader Jaques Wagner, involving allegations of overseas transfers, paid hospitality, and quid-pro-quo arrangements. Despite denials and partial confirmations, the STF upheld the detention of Vorcaro’s relatives, drawing comparisons to Operation Car Wash. Finance Minister Dario Durigan announced efforts to coordinate adjustments with the STF amid the escalating political fallout.

item.title: Governo Tarcísio tem 63,2% de aprovação em SP, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) maintains a 63.2% approval rating in São Paulo, according to a Paraná Pesquisas institute survey, showing a slight negative oscillation within the 2.5-point margin of error. 31.9% of voters disapprove of his administration, while 4.9% were unsure or did not respond.

item.title: Planalto minimiza efeito de condenação de Eduardo na relação com Trump
item.description: The Planalto downplays the potential impact of Eduardo Bolsonaro's STF conviction on Lula's government relations with Donald Trump, arguing that Bolsonarists will always find pretexts to undermine the relationship. Advisors emphasize that the government will maintain direct contact with the Trump administration to counter far-right influence, recalling that past approaches by Bolsonaro family members to Trump have historically led to negative outcomes for Brazil.

item.title: Flávio ataca PT e finge esquecer o próprio tombo no Caso Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro used the Federal Police operation against government leader Jaques Wagner to attack the PT, equating it with the PCC and Comando Vermelho at an event in São Paulo with Sérgio Moro and Guilherme Derrite. Ricardo Noblat criticized the statement as opportunistic and desperate, noting that Flávio is trying to divert attention from his declining poll numbers and his own legal troubles in the Caso Master. The columnist said associating the PT with organized crime is a baseless and cheap provocation.

item.title: Foragido, Léo Índio surge em vídeo próximo à fronteira com o Brasil
item.description: Léo Índio, cousin of former President Jair Bolsonaro’s sons, appeared in a video near the Iguazu Falls on the Argentina-Brazil border, where he has been a fugitive since April 2023 following an arrest warrant issued by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for his role in the January 8 attacks. He has authorization to stay in Argentina and recently filed a petition with the OEA accusing Moraes of persecution. In February 2025, the STF’s First Chamber unanimously accepted the prosecution’s denunciation, making him a defendant in the coup attempt case.

item.title: Estatais: Razões da ineficiência
item.description: President Lula denies that state-owned enterprises are less efficient, arguing their goal is to fill market gaps, not pursue profit. However, the text contends that state-owned inefficiency stems from frequent leadership changes and public procurement rules, citing the successful privatizations of Vale, Telebras, and Embraer as evidence that the private sector enhances productivity and economic growth.

item.title: Michelle vai à convenção do PL que confirmará Flávio como candidato à Presidência?
item.description: The PL national convention will be held on July 25 to officially nominate Flávio Bolsonaro as the party's candidate for president in the 2026 election. The event, exclusive to subscribers, marks the formal launch of the electoral campaign for the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Mendonça busca evitar atritos políticos em operações do caso Master
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça, rapporteur of the Master case, avoided conducting searches inside the Senate during operations targeting Senators Ciro Nogueira and Jaques Wagner to prevent institutional friction between the Judiciary and Legislature. The decision was based on concerns that such actions would pose a high risk of political wear without adding relevant information to the investigation. The article also discusses debates on Eduardo Bolsonaro’s punishment, the use of AI in satirical content and fake news, and the impact of STF rulings on the 2026 elections.

item.title: A eleição de R$ 56 bilhões: por que políticos têm volume recorde de dinheiro neste ano
item.description: The 2015 STF ban on corporate donations to political campaigns shifted electoral financing to public funds, particularly through parliamentary amendments. In 2026, parties and candidates will have access to R$ 56 billion in public resources for campaigns — over ten times the private funding of 2014 — including R$ 7 billion in 'Pix amendments' that lack oversight and enable corruption, as evidenced by the conviction of deputies for extorting bribes in exchange for fund allocation.

item.title: Sozinho contra a direita, Lula calcula o risco dos debates na TV
item.description: The PT campaign is cautiously evaluating Lula's participation in televised debates for the 2026 elections, aiming to balance exposure while avoiding unproductive confrontations. The team plans to compensate for potential absences with sabbaticals and interviews, as debates are now seen less as isolated events and more as raw material for social media content. Three debates have set dates: August 16 on Band, September 14 in a media pool, and September 27 on RecordTV, with a possible one on Globo near the first round.

item.title: Jogadores da seleção brasileira celebram vitória nas redes sociais; veja publicações
item.description: Brazilian national team players celebrated their 3-0 victory over Haiti in the 2026 World Cup on social media. Ten of the 25 available players posted on Instagram, emphasizing team unity, gratitude, and focus ahead of their next match against Scotland. Neymar did not travel for the match.

item.title: Brasil terá rede de proteção aos direitos da pessoa idosa
item.description: Brazil has established a protection network for the rights of older persons, as defined by Ordinance No. 1.058/2026 of the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship. The initiative aims to strengthen coordination between government levels and civil society to ensure access to rights based on equity, non-discrimination, and respect for the diversity of aging. Coordination is assigned to the National Secretariat for the Rights of Older Persons, in partnership with the National Council for the Rights of Older Persons.

item.title: 'Desconvite' a Zema racha o Novo em SC e pressiona aliança com o PL
item.description: The Novo party in Santa Catarina 'uninvited' Romeu Zema from a state party meeting scheduled for early July, prompting complaints from members and public repudiation by municipal directories. The move increases pressure for an alliance between Novo and the PL in the state, as the party faces internal divisions over its electoral strategy for 2026.

item.title: Site oficial de Neymar manda indireta a Lula
item.description: Neymar's official website issued an indirect response to a joke made by President Lula regarding the footballer's absence from Brazil's World Cup match against Haiti. Lula had mocked the call-up by calling Neymar the 'first home office call-up in the world' in a teasing tone. The website's reply came as a counter jab, though the full content of the post is not detailed in the excerpt.

item.title: Investimento em saneamento em SP será o triplo da média nacional
item.description: The 2024 privatization of Sabesp enabled São Paulo to triple its sanitation investment per capita compared to the national average, rising from R$171 to R$369 per inhabitant. With a projected R$70 billion in investments through 2029, the state aims to achieve universal access to treated water and sewage by 2029 — four years ahead of the national 2033 target — and has already met 87% of its water supply goals in Q1 2025.

item.title: Empresa chinesa de biomedicina mira contratos com o SUS
item.description: Haier Biomedical, a subsidiary of the Haier Group, aims to expand in Brazil by targeting SUS contracts, offering intelligent equipment for blood and medicine storage and transport. Operating in Brazil since 2024, it has partnered with HemoRio on the Urban Intelligent Blood Network and expresses interest in joining Brazil’s first smart hospital project in São Paulo, funded by federal, state governments and the BRICS Bank. The company maintains a strong relationship with Health Minister Alexandre Padilha and is awaiting the 2026 election results to finalize its SUS market entry strategy.

item.title: Tarcísio é aprovado por 63,2% e desaprovado por 31,9% em SP, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey conducted between June 16 and 18, 2026, with 1,600 voters across 80 municipalities in São Paulo, shows 63.2% approve of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’ (Republicanos) administration, while 31.9% disapprove. In evaluating the state government, 46.7% rate it as 'excellent' or 'good', compared to 23.6% who rate it as 'bad' or 'terrible'. The poll has a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points and a 95% confidence level, and is registered with the TSE under number SP-08639/2026.

item.title: Pesquisa: gestão Tarcísio é aprovada por 63,2% e reprovada por 31,9%
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' government has 63.2% approval and 31.9% disapproval according to Paraná Pesquisas Institute survey released on June 20, with a 2.5-point margin of error and a slight decline from May (64.4%). Approval is higher among men (68%) than women (59.1%).

item.title: Mendonça manda remover posts que associam Flávio a Vorcaro e milícias
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of social media posts falsely linking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to Daniel Vorcaro and Rio militias, labeling them as AI-manipulated and misleading. He also approved takedowns of content associating Bolsonaro with the 2026 Flexible Work Hours PEC, in response to PL requests. Out of seven rulings, four favored the PL and three the PT, with all decisions to be reviewed by the TSE plenary.

item.title: TSE avalia manter teto de gastos para campanhas em 2026
item.description: The TSE is considering maintaining campaign spending limits for 2026 without inflation adjustment, following the 2022 framework, with R$ 4.9 billion from the Electoral Fund distributed among 30 parties. Parties requested the retention of 2022 spending caps, citing that the Special Campaign Financing Fund also remained unchanged. The PT is set to receive R$ 615 million in 2026, the second-largest allocation among parties, behind only the PL.

item.title: A Colômbia de hoje é o Brasil de 2018 com Bolsonaro, diz CEO da Atlas
item.description: In the first round of Colombia's presidential election on May 31, far-right candidate Abelardo De la Espriella surprised by leading with 43.7% of the vote, surpassing leftist Iván Cepeda, who received 40.90%. The CEO of Atlas compares this scenario to Brazil in 2018, when Jair Bolsonaro similarly emerged as an unexpected far-right leader amid polarization and popular discontent.

item.title: Especialistas defendem debate sobre regra para pesquisas, mas temem restrição excessiva a institutos
item.description: Electoral law and political science experts advocate for clearer regulation of electoral polls to prevent voter induction, particularly regarding government approval, voting intention, and rejection questions, while warning against excessive restrictions that could hinder polling institutes. The TSE is studying parameters following the suspension of an AtlasIntel poll, focusing on question order and establishing an objective distinction between inducement and legitimate questioning. Ministers such as Dias Toffoli and André Mendonça stressed that the limit must not be subjective or biased.

item.title: TSE vai debater regras de pesquisas e retomar julgamento sobre pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro em agosto
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will resume its judgment on Flávio Bolsonaro’s request regarding the AtlasIntel poll in August, after consulting polling institutes in July to establish objective criteria for electoral poll impartiality. The suspension of the poll’s release by TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques sparked internal debate over the subjectivity of electoral justice decisions. The goal is to prevent future rulings from relying on individual judges’ assessments and to set clear rules for campaigns starting August 16.

item.title: Caso Master chega ao governo e impõe dilema a Lula antes de campanha
item.description: The Federal Police operation against Jaques Wagner, Lula's Senate leader, has created a political crisis for the president, with suspicions that Wagner received improper benefits from the Master scheme. Despite internal pressure for him to step down, Wagner says Lula expressed support and that he will remain in his leadership role and Senate pre-candidacy. Lula’s public silence, combined with a thumbs-up gesture in Minas Gerais, keeps tensions high within the government base less than two months before the electoral campaign.

item.title: Lula aposta em diálogo político com a UE para reverter veto à carne
item.description: The Lula government is seeking to reverse the European Union's veto on Brazilian beef imports by shifting to a more political and diplomatic approach after the EU excluded Brazil from its list of authorized exporters in May. The strategy involves establishing a direct channel between Itamaraty and the EU to address sanitary concerns without challenging technical standards, aiming to prevent the measure from being perceived as protectionist. The EU has also imposed restrictions on steel and soybean oil exports, effective July 1, which Brazil views as having political motivations beyond commercial grounds.

item.title: Messi ou Cristiano Ronaldo? Estudo aponta qual dos craques é favorito entre pessoas de esquerda ou direita; entenda
item.description: A study of 10,661 respondents across 26 countries, including Brazil, found that political identity is the most consistent factor explaining preference between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo: left-leaning individuals tend to favor Messi, associated with a discreet, family-oriented, collectivist image, while conservatives favor Ronaldo, seen as a symbol of individual affirmation and self-confidence. Other factors, such as approval of authoritarian attitudes and short-form video news consumption, predicted preference for Ronaldo, while cognitive reflection showed a weak link to Messi.

item.title: TSE faz acordo com partidos para evitar fraudes de cotas para mulheres, pretos e indígenas; veja casos polêmicos
item.description: The TSE has reached an agreement with political parties to ensure compliance with gender, race, and ethnicity quotas in the 2026 elections, aiming to prevent frauds like those recorded in 2022. The article highlights controversial cases, including ACM Neto’s racial self-declaration in Bahia and an alleged gender quota fraud in Amapá involving the Podemos party. The rules mandate at least 30% female candidacies and allocate 30% of electoral funds to Black candidates, with proportional distribution for Indigenous candidates.

item.title: País sem projeto, candidatos sem rumo
item.description: Brazil lacks a long-term national project, with politicians focused only on the next election. This absence of strategic vision is a recurring criticism, but requires deeper analysis of its structural causes.

item.title: Especialistas veem como avanço exigência de nota mínima no Enamed para exercício da Medicina
item.description: President Lula's provisional measure establishes a minimum 60% score on the Enamed exam as a requirement to practice medicine, similar to the OAB exam for lawyers, applying only to students entering medical school from now on. The rule will take full effect in mid-2032, when the first affected cohort graduates. Experts view the change positively, as it will evaluate both students and medical schools' educational quality.

item.title: Da defensiva ao ataque: como operação contra líder do PT modificou postura de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre caso Master
item.description: The Federal Police operation targeting PT Senate leader Jaques Wagner eased pressure on Flávio Bolsonaro, who had previously borne alone the political cost of the Master Bank scandal. Bolsonaro then began publicly advocating for a CPMI to investigate the bank, attempting to link the scandal to the PT and shift blame. Though allies acknowledge the issue remains a liability, the operation allowed him to retaliate in kind, moving from defense to offense.

item.title: Acabou a química: na mesma semana, Trump chamou política do Brasil de 'difícil' e Lula, de 'volátil'
item.description: In the same week, U.S. President Donald Trump criticized Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, calling him 'very volatile' and saying he 'could not care less' about him. Earlier at the G7 in France, Trump had described Brazil as a 'politically difficult country'. These remarks contrast sharply with Trump’s earlier praise of an 'excellent chemistry' with Lula in September 2023, signaling a notable deterioration in bilateral relations.

item.title: Com Flávio e Tarcísio, André do Prado lança pré-candidatura ao Senado
item.description: State deputy André do Prado (PL-SP) launched his Senate pre-candidacy in an event with Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, on the governor's reelection ticket. The candidacy faces challenges after the first alternate, Eduardo Bolsonaro, was declared ineligible by the STF, though André maintains Eduardo as his alternate and Fernando Fiori de Godoy as second alternate. The event was framed as the launch of the 'united right' strategy, with symbolic appeal and local mobilization.

item.title: Políticos comemoram 1ª vitória da seleção brasileira na Copa
item.description: Brazilian politicians celebrated the national team's 3-0 victory over Haiti in the 2026 World Cup via social media, praising the team's performance and commenting on players like Neymar and Endrick. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) called Neymar a 'craque' and criticized President Lula for luxury travel expenses, while Erika Hilton (Psol-SP), Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), Renan Santos (Missão-SP), and Guilherme Boulos (Psol-SP) also celebrated the win and shared their correct score predictions.
